items.title: George "Jug" Jernberg Interview, 1963-08-23
items.q: And Charlie Thorpe played piano there for the singers

ctx.x: Wadsworth was the guy that, uh, really booked the job and landed the job and hired Kelly as the banjo player. So from then on, uh, uh, Kelly, and it was, I guess it was Erking Wadsworth pretty much. And they, if Wadsworth probably was out of there and that's when Kelly got Gus Miller to come in to play clarinet and tenor saxophone. And he, uh, Gus. And the band had broken up. And that's what broke up the band. Uh, Ray Lopez, uh, went with another band over at the, uh, Windcliff Inn. I told you about that too, I…

Salisbury were a singing trio in the Windcliffe Inn, and Ray Lopez was in the band that played for dancing down there. And Ray Lopez's father was the clarinet player. He could play the New Orleans style clarinet fairly well, you know, nothing to brag about. Ray Lopez, yeah. And Charlie Thorpe played piano there for the singers, and Earl, what the heck was his name, Earl Chigrew or some such name as that, played piano with the dance band. And then later on when Benny Fields married Blossom Sealy, Ray Lopez went…
That's how they got... Well, what do you say about Ray Lopez being the best of the early Dixieland trumpet players is supported by, say, Frankie Quartel, for example. He swears by Lopez.
